intentAndPurpose.intent: Text-only toggle button for binary selection — no start/end slots, simpler than SelectableButton.

rules.name: high attention
useWhen: selected state needs bold fill emphasis

rules.name: medium attention
useWhen: selected state with subtle tinted fill

rules.name: low attention
useWhen: selected state with ghost appearance and accent border

props.name: children
props.description: Text label content — max 2 characters (e.g. "Ag", "En", "A", "12"). This component renders as a circular button; longer text breaks the shape. Text exceeding 2 characters will be truncated in development with a warning.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible label for screen readers (optional — children text is visible)

props.name: attention
props.description: Attention level — determines the visual prominence of the SELECTED state. high → bold fill; medium → subtle fill; low → ghost with accent border. The UNSELECTED state is always muted ghost regardless of attention. Default: 'high'.

props.name: condensed
props.description: Condensed mode: reduces height and horizontal padding while keeping the same typography.

props.name: data-testid
props.description: QA / e2e anchor on the root toggle element

props.name: loading
props.description: Loading state — shows circular progress indicator replacing the text label. Disables interaction while loading.

props.name: selected
props.description: Selected state (controlled). Maps to Toggle pressed.

props.name: size
props.description: Button size. Default: 'm'. S/M/L only (no XS).

interactionBehavior.summary: SelectableSingleTextButton is a Base UI Toggle for a 1–2 character circular label, so every click flips `aria-pressed` and it starts UNSELECTED. Attention colours the SELECTED look only; unselected is always a muted ghost with a `--{Role}-Stroke-Low` hairline. It scales UP on press (`--Motion-Tap-Scale-Up`, 7%) with NO pressed fill token — the same grow-not-squash direction as SelectableIconButton, opposite SelectableButton. There is no `contained={false}`. `loading` implies disabled and injects a spinner, but the CSS that would hide the letters is keyed off a `.loading` class the component never applies, so the characters stay visible beside the spinner.
hover: Every hover rule is wrapped in `@media (hover: hover)` and excluded for `[data-disabled]`.
UNSELECTED tints the transparent rest fill to `--{Role}-Hover`.

SELECTED at `attention="high"` steps the fill to `--{Role}-Bold-Hover` (or keeps `--{Role}-Material-Fill`); at `medium` it steps to `--{Role}-Subtle-Hover`; at `low` it ADDS a `--{Role}-Hover` fill over the rest transparent-plus-accent-hairline.
Label colour never changes on hover — only the background.
press: The whole circle scales UP: `scale(calc(1 + var(--_tap-direction) * var(--_tap-scale) / 100))` with `--Motion-Tap-Scale-Up` at 7%. SelectableButton scales DOWN; this matches IconButton and SelectableIconButton.
There is no `:active` fill, border, or text-colour rule — the scale-up is the entire pressed look.
Press is NOT `(hover: hover)`-guarded, so a finger tap gets the same grow a mouse press does.
focus: Keyboard focus draws the two-layer halo: an inner `--Stroke-XL` gap ring in `--Surface-Halo-Gap` plus an outer `--Focus-Outline` ring.
`:focus` alone only clears the native outline; the visible ring is `:focus-visible`.
keyboard: Base UI Toggle renders a native `<button aria-pressed>`, so `Enter` and `Space` both toggle.
Controlled via `selected` / `onSelectedChange`; uncontrolled via `defaultSelected` (unset → unselected). Pass `value` when nesting inside a ToggleGroup.
Disabled and loading are natively `disabled`, so they are out of the tab order and cannot toggle — covered by a unit test.
selected: Selected maps to Base UI Toggle's `pressed`, exposed as `aria-pressed` and matched in CSS with `[data-pressed]`.
It defaults to unselected in uncontrolled mode.

`attention` colours the SELECTED look only: high → `--{Role}-Bold` fill with `--{Role}-Bold-High` text and a transparent border; medium → `--{Role}-Subtle` fill with `--{Role}-TintedA11y` text; low → transparent fill with a `--{Role}-Bold` hairline and accent text.
Unselected is always transparent + `--{Role}-Medium-Text` + `--{Role}-Stroke-Low` hairline, ignoring attention — there is no uncontained variant to change that.
loading: `loading` implies disabled — `isDisabled = disabled || loading` — so the native `disabled` attribute is set, `aria-busy` / `data-loading` are set, and `onSelectedChange` stops firing.

A spinner is injected as a sibling of the still-rendered label. The CSS that would hide that label (`.loading .label { opacity: 0 }`) and absolutely centre the spinner is keyed off a `.loading` class that SelectableSingleTextButton never applies, so the letters stay visible beside the spinner and the circle can grow.
Tests only assert that a spinner SVG is present and that the toggle is blocked — they do not assert the label is hidden.
disabled: `data-disabled` dims to `--Disabled-Opacity` and sets `cursor: not-allowed` plus `pointer-events: none`.

Because the element is natively `disabled` AND has `pointer-events: none`, the `not-allowed` cursor is not observable — the pointer shows the parent's cursor. Known, accepted system-wide gap (see docs/design/disabled-states.md).
Hover fills and the tap-scale are qualified with `:not([data-disabled])`. Disabling does not clear the selected styling — it only dims it.
touch: Hover fills never apply on touch-only devices; the 7% scale-up is the entire visual response to a tap, because there is no pressed fill.
Growing on press is the right direction for a control this small — the circle expands out from under the fingertip that is covering the letters.
